original_question: For integers n and d with 3 <= d <= n + 1, is every smooth degree d hypersurface in projective space P^{n+1} K-stable?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 6: prove that every smooth hypersurface of degree 3 \le d \le n+1 in \mathbb{P}^{n+1} is K-stable.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content of the paper-faithful problem: it asks about all smooth degree-d hypersurfaces in \mathbb{P}^{n+1}, uses the correct degree range 3 \le d \le n+1, and asks for K-stability rather than a broader neighboring property such as K-semistability or description of moduli.
missing_details: The paper phrases this as a problem about a hypersurface X \subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}; naming X explicitly makes the question fully stand-alone.
The ground field is left implicit in your draft; in the paper's K-stability setting this is understood to be the usual characteristic-0 setting, typically over \mathbb{C}.
The inequality d \le n+1 is not just a numerical bound: it is exactly the Fano range for a smooth hypersurface in \mathbb{P}^{n+1}, so the intended meaning is K-stability of X as a Fano variety.
To avoid ambiguity, it helps to say explicitly that K-stability is the anticanonical/Fano notion for X.
The universal quantifier on n is implicit in your wording; making clear that n is arbitrary subject to 3 \le d \le n+1 improves stand-alone precision.
refined_question: Let X \subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}_{\mathbb{C}} be a smooth hypersurface of degree d, where 3 \le d \le n+1. Is X K-stable as a Fano variety?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every smooth hypersurface X \subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}_{\mathbb{C}} of degree d with 3 \le d \le n+1, does one have \delta(X)>1, where \delta(X) is the stability threshold?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. The nearest official formulation is Problem 6 in Section 2, which asks exactly about smooth Fano hypersurfaces. I therefore kept the scope on smooth hypersurfaces in projective space and did not broaden it to moduli questions or complete intersections. The only refinements are to make the hypersurface X explicit, supply the usual base field, and clarify that the K-stability in question is the standard Fano/anticanonical notion. The alternate formulation is justified by Theorem 2 in the same section, which gives the equivalence between K-stability and the strict inequality \delta(X)>1 for log Fano pairs.
